approved: Said Labor does not oppose the Anti-Dumping Commission Transfer Bill, which builds on Labor's $27.7 million package of antidumping reforms and a broader $1 billion Industry and Innovation Statement now at risk of coalition cuts, and cited Tindo Solar in his Makin electorate as a local manufacturer being undercut by dumped Chinese solar panels.

Supported the Anti-Dumping Commission Transfer Bill, used Vegemite pricing to show Australians pay about 32 per cent more than New Zealanders due to higher local retail costs rather than dumping, cited a KPMG report showing supermarket trade spend rose from 19 to 24 per cent of sales, and warned the carbon tax pushes aluminium production to China, where a tonne of aluminium emits 1.35 tonnes of CO2 compared with 0.85 tonnes in Australia.

Argued the Customs Amendment Anti-Dumping Commission Transfer Bill 2013 is needed to strengthen antidumping protections, citing SPC Ardmona's case against dumped Italian tomatoes that resulted in duties of six to nine per cent, and criticised Australia's weighted-average method of calculating dumping margins as weaker than New Zealand's approach, noting Heinz closed its Girgarre tomato sauce factory, which employed about 90 people, and moved production to New Zealand.

Summed up debate on the bill transferring the Anti-Dumping Commission to the Department of Industry, noting manufacturing employment fell from 1,038,500 to 921,400 between the 2002 to 2003 and 2012 to 2013 financial years, and said antidumping investigations rose by around 34 per cent between 2011 to 2012 and 2012 to 2013, thanking members for their contributions to the debate.

The speech announced the transfer of the Anti-Dumping Commission to the Department of Industry, changes to social security including a 35-year Australian working life residence requirement for overseas pensioners and a $7,500 annual child care rebate cap, and amendments to submarine cable protection legislation to align with UNCLOS and streamline permit processes.

Moved to schedule non-controversial government bills for consideration from 12:45 pm, including amendments to the Australian Civilian Corps, Import Processing Charges, Grape and Wine Authority, Offshore Petroleum, Rural Research and Development, and Customs Anti-Dumping Commission. Also moved to set general business order for the day, prioritising Senator Moore's motion on pre-election commitments and government document orders.

The speaker opposed transferring the Anti-Dumping Commission to the department, citing the Brumby review’s concerns about investigative powers and integrity standards, and asked how department staff would meet the same thresholds as customs officers. He also reiterated support for reversing the onus of proof in dumping cases.
